subject.title: Feature request: Persistent task-status surface for long-running channel turns

question: What canonical owner and contract should define persistent channel-turn status for long-running chat runs?
rationale: The remaining work affects runtime lifecycle semantics, channel message editing, persistence after restart, config policy, and the relationship between progress drafts, task records, and gateway activity APIs; automation cannot safely pick that product boundary.

options.title: Add Runtime-Owned Status Contract
options.body: Approve a narrow additive status contract with durable ownership, unknown/interrupted fallback, and Discord-first best-effort transport while keeping final reply delivery independent.

options.title: Defer Behind Gateway Activity API
options.body: Wait for the broader per-session activity API work to settle, then project that canonical activity state into channel-visible status messages.

options.title: Keep Progress Drafts Only
options.body: Decline a separate persistent terminal status surface for now and rely on progress drafts, task records, and channel busy snapshots as the supported UX.

recommendation.title: Add Runtime-Owned Status Contract
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow additive status contract with durable ownership, unknown/interrupted fallback, and Discord-first best-effort transport while keeping final reply delivery independent.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Discord/channel draft transport and task/status boundary work makes this the best available routing owner for deciding whether the feature belongs in runtime, channel, gateway, or task surfaces.
